hook_text: A lion has an address, just like your house. Country, province, city, street — scientists use seven lines.
clip_script: Your home has an address. Country, province, city, suburb, street, house. Each line narrows it down. Living things have one too. Kingdom: Animals. Phylum: Chordata, animals with backbones. Class: Mammalia, hair and milk. Order: Carnivora, meat-eaters. Family: Felidae, the cats. Genus: Panthera, the roaring big cats. Species: leo. The lion. King Philip Came Over For Good Soup. Now the cool part. Its scientific name, Panthera leo, works like surname first. The leopard is Panthera pardus. Same surname, close cousins. And whether you say ingonyama, tau, leeu or lion, a scientist anywhere in the world knows exactly which animal Panthera leo means.
visual_style: A whiteboard envelope whose address lines turn into the seven classification levels, zooming from a crowd of animals down to a single lion; then two name tags side by side, Panthera leo and Panthera pardus.
pacing: Steady seven-step zoom, a quick surname reveal, a confident finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how closely you are related to a lion.
